pr_body:
Fixes #8206.

Since #8206 is a long-awaited (~ 1 year old), popular (~ 45 reactions, frequently requested in community channels, etc.), this PR aims to unblock folks.

Notably, we do not innovate on the `webServer` API, despite knowing we're not in love with it. We'll save the innovation for either Plugins or a new `LaunchConfigs` option. (We haven't yet arrived at a Plugin API we like, and instead of launching a new option guessing what the "better" launchConfig API would be, let's wait and see how folks use this new Array-variant of `webServer` which—despite its name—can be used for non-Web Server launches!

issue_context.title: [Feature]: Support launching multiple web servers
issue_context.body:
**Context:**
- GOOD Playwright Version: 1.13
- BAD Playwright Version: 1.14
- Operating System: Mac (didn't test other OS)
- Extra: N/A

**Code Snippet**

This used to work on 1.13 (updated to 1.14 option names). 

```javascript
const config: PlaywrightTestConfig = {
  webServer: [
    {
      command: 'yarn workspace @app/graphql start',
      port: 4000, 
      timeout: 60000,
      reuseExistingServer: !isCI,
    },
    {
      command: 'yarn workspace @app/frontend start',
      port: 3000, 
      timeout: 60000,
      reuseExistingServer: !isCI,
    }
  ]
};
```

**Describe the bug**

Previously we had the experimental `_launch` option to start a server for tests, and this options accepted an array of several servers to start. With 1.14 released it was renamed to `webServer` and only takes one server as a parameter. Maybe it's a weird use case but it was really helpful to be able to lift several servers. `baseUrl` fixture took the value of the last server launched.

Would it be possible to add this back?
comments:
This would be really helpful for us as well.

We would like to start
1) Our API server
2) Our Frontend "server" (next js)

Which are both needed to have a full environment to e2e test.

I had to skip one of our tests and fixing this would help. Let's bring back the launch configurations exactly as it was:
- multiple values
- no automatic baseURL assignment
- explicit request to wait for port

We probably don't need to deprecate `webServer` property for now, those can co-exist.

We have a situation where only sometimes we want to start a webserver.  We point to a "live' system or our 'development server'.  So it would be nice if the webserver can be referenced or added in the "project" section and not just at the top level of the config.  This way I could have some projects start a webserver and other's point to a 'live' system instead.

Makes sense to me as well. In my case, I want to test authenticated scenarios with real auth services, but rest of tests - with auth fully mocked. So I thought starting separate servers with different build configs for that - would totally make sense.

Right now the only alternative - to use separate playwright.config, which does not allow to have single test result.

https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/11141
What I have asked here is kind different but it's related to this issue
We also needed different server configs for multiple projects, any chance that this feature will be implemented?
Same thing here. One of the reasons I choose Playwright, is to test how different websites interact (e.g. create a company in an admin panel, see the company live in the web app)
Maybe passing an array of `ports` could be a simpler alternative 😄
This looks interesting, I think it would be nice if the server could  depend on another. E.g. wait for server-1 to have started before server 2 or something similar
I need this as well!  In my case I was happy with passing in an array of web servers to start.
Any suggestions for any workarounds in the meantime?
Re-openeing and moving to v1.23; this was implemented atop plugins which will not be in 1.22.

If the Webserver code is being overhauled to allow launching multiple webservers, this might be a good opportunity to look at https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/12299 and make sure they can also be closed properly (allowing them to clean up open DB connections, etc). Currently webserver processes on Linux get rather abruptly terminated, with no chance to do any cleanup work.
